In plain words

A researcher showed that hidden text inside a Word document can make Microsoft 365 Copilot change numbers in a report and secretly copy the same hidden instructions into the new file it creates. This affects people and organizations using Copilot in Word when outside documents or OneDrive files are included in Copilot’s drafting or editing work. It matters because an ordinary-looking, internally created document could later carry the same hidden instructions into another Copilot session, making the unwanted changes harder to trace even though the issue does not spread by itself or run malware.

Summary
A researcher found that hidden prompts in Word documents can cause Microsoft 365 Copilot to alter report data and copy the concealed instructions into newly generated files, allowing the prompt-injection behavior to carry into later Copilot sessions. Microsoft deployed mitigations, but the researcher says the broader attack class remains exploitable and requires users to treat external and Copilot-generated documents as untrusted.

Håkon Måløy disclosed a technique showing that hidden instructions in a Word document can make Microsoft 365 Copilot rewrite figures in a report and copy the same instructions into the finished file. In his proof of concept, an internally generated file triggered the same behavior when used in a second Copilot drafting session. The disclosure says there is no reported exploitation in the wild, and Måløy withheld the complete payload.

The attack requires a Copilot drafting or editing operation, and the malicious document must enter the model’s context as an attachment or as a OneDrive source selected by Work IQ. In the proof of concept, Copilot halved every financial figure, copied the full prompt into the output in white, eight-point text, and disclosed neither change. Måløy said Word strips colour and font size before sending document text to the large language model, leaving white-on-white instructions legible to the model.

Microsoft confirmed the reported behavior on March 31 and deployed two mitigations, including blocking the original prompt wording and upgrading the underlying model to GPT-5.5. Måløy said modified instructions still worked on GPT-5.6 the next day and that the attack class still reproduced on July 28. The article says no public CVE or standalone Microsoft advisory was found for the Word finding at publication time, and Måløy recommends treating external documents as untrusted and reviewing Copilot-generated or edited files before reuse or sharing.

  • Word strips color and font size before sending document text to the model, which can make visually hidden white-on-white instructions readable to Copilot.
  • The second-stage carrier can be an ordinary internally generated document, so the original malicious source may no longer be present when the behavior repeats.
  • Work IQ can expand exposure beyond files a user intentionally attaches, because it may select a relevant OneDrive source from outside the folder containing the other sources.
  • Payload-specific blocking may be insufficient for this issue because Måløy reported that modified instructions reproduced the same attack class after Microsoft’s mitigations.

In plain words

Silent Push studied thousands of forgotten web addresses from government and Fortune 500 organizations and showed that many could be taken over because they still pointed to online services that no longer existed. This could let criminals put fake login pages or harmful content under a trusted organization’s name, making scams much harder to spot. The affected groups include government agencies, banks, pharmaceutical companies, automakers, and other major industries, with possible real-world consequences ranging from stolen credentials to disruptions in public services, banking, supply chains, and health research.

Summary
Silent Push simulated large-scale dangling DNS and subdomain takeovers across government and Fortune 500 environments, showing that abandoned cloud-linked records can quickly become trusted launchpads for phishing, credential theft, and broader compromise. The key defense is continuous DNS monitoring and strict decommissioning hygiene: remove or reclaim DNS records before deleting the cloud resources they point to.

Silent Push conducted a research initiative called “Danglegeddon” to simulate large-scale exploitation of dangling DNS infrastructure across government and Fortune 500 organizations. The team targeted 12,500 apex domains, isolated 16,000 dangling subdomains, and automated the takeover of 4,000 of them in a controlled environment. The research initially focused on Microsoft infrastructure, including Azure Blobs, Azure VMs, Web Apps, APIs, and Power Pages instances.

The article explains that a taken-over subdomain is not itself an intrusion, but it can become a trusted launchpad for phishing pages, credential-harvesting forms, malicious content, OAuth redirection, or, in some misconfigured cases, interception of shared session tokens. Silent Push modeled potential impacts across government, banking, pharmaceutical, and automotive sectors, highlighting how trusted but abandoned infrastructure could affect public agencies, financial services, drug development, supply chains, and major manufacturers. The article says the ultimate severity depends on additional security failures such as weak multi-factor authentication, broad internal trust, or overly broad cookie scoping.

Silent Push describes dangling CNAME, MX, and NS records as carrying different risks, with dangling NS records presented as the worst because control of a delegated name server can affect an entire zone. The article says its platform finds dangling records through daily re-resolution of hostnames rather than one-off scans, allowing defenders to see added, removed, and unchanged exposures. It recommends fixing records in order of blast radius, deleting or correctly repointing abandoned DNS entries, reclaiming claimable resources defensively when needed, and ensuring DNS records are removed before cloud resources during decommissioning.

  • The article emphasizes that dangling DNS becomes far more dangerous when combined with other common hygiene failures, such as broad cookie scoping, weak multi-factor authentication, overly broad internal trust, or trusted third-party relationships.
  • Silent Push found that provider-side safeguards materially reduce takeover risk, citing 4,925 records that were not claimable because protections such as domain ownership verification were in place.
  • The article frames daily re-resolution of hostnames as more effective than target-specific scanning because forgotten records often do not appear in an organization’s own asset inventories or past testing scopes.
  • The recommended remediation order is based on blast radius rather than volume: dangling NS records should be addressed before MX records, external CNAMEs, and internal records, even though CNAMEs were far more common in the study.
  • The research links organizational change events such as employee attrition, layoffs, and mergers or acquisitions to orphaned DNS exposure, making DNS review an actionable part of change control and termination processes.
Key Points
  • 01Silent Push analyzed 12,500 apex domains from government and Fortune 500 organizations and identified 16,000 dangling subdomains, with automated takeover of 4,000 of them in a controlled simulation.
  • 02The simulation used dangling DNS takeover to demonstrate how abandoned DNS records could enable credential harvesting, OAuth redirection, phishing pages, cookie theft in some misconfigured cases, and abuse of trusted organizational domains.
  • 03Silent Push focused initially on Microsoft infrastructure, including Azure Blobs, Azure VMs, Web Apps, APIs, and Power Pages instances, and found takeover examples across government, banking, automotive, and pharmaceutical organizations.
  • 04The article states that dangling CNAME, MX, and NS records carry different risks, with dangling NS records described as the worst because control of the delegated name server can allow control over the entire zone beneath it.
  • 05Silent Push recommends deleting or correctly repointing dangling records, reclaiming claimable resources defensively where needed, removing DNS records before cloud resources during decommissioning, using domain ownership verification, assigning record owners, publishing CAA records, and continuously monitoring DNS changes.

In plain words

The FCC added foreign-produced mobile robots and networked power inverters to a list that generally blocks new models from being imported, marketed, or sold in the US. People who already own these devices and previously approved models are not affected, and those devices can still receive security and compatibility updates. The concern is that remotely connected robots and power inverters could be misused to spy, shut down equipment, steal data, or threaten parts of the electric grid, even though the FCC did not identify an active campaign currently exploiting them.

Summary
The FCC added foreign-produced mobile robots and networked power inverters to its Covered List, blocking most new models from import, marketing, or sale in the US over preventive cyber and supply-chain risk concerns. Existing devices and previously authorized models are not affected, and security/compatibility updates remain allowed under a waiver.

The Federal Communications Commission added foreign-produced mobile robots and networked power inverters to its Covered List on July 28. The action generally prevents new models from receiving the equipment authorization required for import, marketing, or sale in the US. Previously authorized models can still be sold, devices people already own are unaffected, and federal purchases and use are not affected by this FCC action.

The FCC also granted a waiver through at least January 1, 2029, for software and firmware changes that patch vulnerabilities and support compatibility with different operating systems. Manufacturers can apply for Conditional Approval by January 1, 2028, with the Department of War able to approve robotic devices and the Department of War or Department of Homeland Security able to approve power inverters. Coverage is based on production and technical tests rather than a list of named manufacturers or countries, and “foreign-produced” is tied to whether an article qualifies as a domestic end product under the Buy American standard.

The robot definition covers certain mobile ground devices over 4.4 lbs that have sensors, support communications of 200 kbps or faster, and run software, firmware, or AI or machine-learning model weights for movement, perception, data collection, or remote command and control. The inverter definition covers systems that convert direct current to alternating current, or the reverse, and include components for remote communication, control, sensing, data collection, or monitoring. The FCC framed the move as a preventive supply-chain action and did not identify a confirmed active exploitation campaign against deployed robots or inverters.

  • The robot definition is broader than humanoids and quadrupeds because it can cover any non-excluded ground-mobile device over 4.4 lbs with sensors, communications of at least 200 kbps, and software that controls movement, perception, data collection, or remote command functions.
  • The FCC explicitly includes firmware and artificial intelligence or machine-learning model weights in the robot software requirement, so model or firmware changes may be relevant to whether a device falls within the covered category.
  • The same FCC action that restricts new authorizations also grants a waiver through at least January 1, 2029, for software and firmware changes that patch vulnerabilities or maintain operating-system compatibility, reducing the risk that covered status blocks security maintenance for already authorized hardware.
  • Coverage depends on Buy American “domestic end product” status and technical characteristics rather than a list of named manufacturers or countries, so companies cannot determine impact solely by checking whether a brand appears in the FCC package.
  • The inverter determination treats remote access as a critical risk even without citing an observed grid disruption, relying on research about flaws, supply-chain concerns, worst-case grid-collapse analysis, and a case where a foreign manufacturer remotely disabled inverters after a distributor dispute.
Key Points
  • 01The FCC added foreign-produced mobile robots and networked power inverters to its Covered List on July 28, generally preventing new models from receiving the equipment authorization required for import, marketing, or sale in the US.
  • 02Previously authorized models can still be sold, devices people already own are unaffected, and qualifying security and compatibility updates may continue under an FCC waiver through at least January 1, 2029.
  • 03Manufacturers can apply for Conditional Approval by January 1, 2028, with the Department of War able to approve robotic devices and the Department of War or Department of Homeland Security able to approve power inverters.
  • 04The FCC’s determinations define coverage by production and technical criteria rather than by brand or named country, and “foreign-produced” means an article that does not qualify as a domestic end product under the Buy American standard.
  • 05The FCC package describes the action as preventive and does not identify a confirmed active exploitation campaign against deployed robots or inverters.

A phishing email impersonating Interactive Brokers used a same-day registered domain hidden behind a Cloudflare challenge to evade automated link scanners while luring recipients to renew a fake W-8BEN tax form. The key lesson is that “clean” link-wrapper verdicts are unreliable when the final destination is a brand-new, inspection-resistant domain.

An email impersonating Interactive Brokers told recipients that their W-8BEN tax form had expired and pushed them to click a “Renew W-8BEN Certification” button. Hook developers must still validate who can call privileged paths, which pools are legitimate, how custom balances and deltas are accounted for, and whether external integrations can fail or reenter safely.

AI-generated scripting is described as a newer pattern, with about 15.6% of active scripts generated by AI and about 13.9% of classified script-using tenants falling into an AI-heavy cohort. Inside that cohort, about 74.4% of scripts are AI-generated, and the article says AI use appears to substitute for cloning rather than simply add to it. It reports average clone share of about 26.5% in AI-heavy tenants, 41.7% in AI-mixed tenants, and 55.9% in no-AI tenants, concluding that cloning-primary operations need source governance while AI-primary operations need output verification.

  • The highest-risk reuse pattern is concentrated: a defect in one of a small number of widely cloned Acronis built-in PowerShell templates could propagate across many tenants because the top six templates account for about 32.5% of all clone copies.
  • Even the most widely trusted cloned templates have incomplete governance, with only about 63.5% to 78.8% of clones marked approved despite every one of the top six carrying credentials in at least some tenant copies.
  • AI adoption changes the required control model rather than simply adding another authoring tool, because AI-heavy tenants clone substantially less and therefore need stronger output verification rather than only stronger template curation.
  • Organizations in AI-augmentation markets such as Australia, Singapore, and the United Kingdom face a heavier governance burden because they combine significant AI use with continued heavy cloning, requiring controls for both generated scripts and reused templates.
  • The article’s practical recommendation is to choose a primary scripting strategy where possible, because few organizations are likely to manage both source-curation discipline for clones and output-verification discipline for AI-generated scripts well from the start.

Talos’ Q2 2026 incident response trends show phishing and authentication abuse surging, with attackers using QR codes, MFA-bypass platforms, and legitimate remote management tools to blend in before ransomware attacks. Talos released its Q2 2026 Incident Response Trends report, which showed a major spike in authentication abuse and sophisticated phishing tactics. Phishing drove over half of all engagements, with attackers using QR codes and advanced platforms like ARToken to bypass multi-factor authentication. A Cosmos master key is a powerful secret key that can grant broad access to an Azure Cosmos DB account.
CosmosEscape vulnerability
CosmosEscape is a named Azure Cosmos DB-related vulnerability or attack technique referenced in security reporting.

COVID-19 pandemic concept
The COVID-19 pandemic was the worldwide outbreak of the COVID-19 disease caused by the coronavirus SARS-CoV-2.

Crafted query technique
A crafted query is a specially prepared request designed to trigger a bug or unusual behavior in a system.
credential abuse technique
Credential abuse is the misuse of usernames, passwords, tokens, or other login secrets to access accounts or systems.

Credential access means trying to steal usernames, passwords, tokens, or other login secrets.
credential collection technique
The process of harvesting usernames, passwords, and tokens, typically by malware or phishing, to gain unauthorized access.
credential harvest technique
Credential harvest is the act of collecting usernames, passwords, tokens, or other login secrets from victims.
also: secret collection
credential rotation technique
Credential rotation means replacing passwords, keys, or tokens with new ones to reduce the risk from stolen or old credentials.
credential theft technique
Credential theft is the stealing of usernames, passwords, tokens, or other login information.
credential-harvesting

also: credential-harvesting forms, Steal user credentials
credential-harvesting page technique
A credential-harvesting page is a fake login page designed to steal usernames and passwords.
credential-stuffing technique
Credential stuffing is when attackers try stolen usernames and passwords on many websites to see where they still work.
credentials concept
Credentials are login details or access tokens that prove a user or system is allowed to access something.
Cresta organization
Cresta is a company that provides artificial intelligence tools for contact centers and customer service.
Criminal justice system organization
The criminal justice system is the set of police, courts, prisons, and agencies that handle crime and punishment.
Critical Cyber Systems Protection Act other
The Critical Cyber Systems Protection Act is a proposed or enacted law focused on protecting important computer systems from cyber threats.
critical infrastructure concept
Critical infrastructure refers to essential systems and services that societies and organizations depend on.
critical infrastructure operators organization
Critical infrastructure operators are organizations that run essential services such as power, water, transport, or communications.

Critical remote code execution is a severe security flaw that lets an attacker run code on a system from afar.
critical vulnerabilities vulnerability
Critical vulnerabilities are very serious security flaws that could let attackers cause major damage or gain major access.

CRM stands for customer relationship management, which refers to systems and data used to manage sales and customer interactions.
CRM records concept
CRM records are customer or business-contact entries stored in customer relationship management systems.

cross-site scripting flaw vulnerability

Cross-tenant reuse means the same credential, key, configuration, or resource is reused across separate customer environments, which can increase risk.

crypto-js product

CryptoCore threat-actor
CryptoCore is a named threat-actor group known in security reporting for cryptocurrency-focused attacks.
cryptocurrency concept
Cryptocurrency is digital money, such as Bitcoin, that uses cryptography and usually runs on a blockchain.
cryptocurrency exchanges organization
Cryptocurrency exchanges are online services where people buy, sell, or trade digital currencies like Bitcoin.
cryptocurrency miner tool
A cryptocurrency miner is software or hardware that performs calculations to earn cryptocurrency, sometimes installed by attackers without permission.
cryptocurrency wallets product
Cryptocurrency wallets are tools used to store and manage access to digital currency funds.

A cryptographic identifier is a mathematically generated value used to uniquely recognize data, a key, or an identity.
also: unique digital signature

CSCwt95974 is a Cisco bug identifier used to track a specific product issue.

cubepilot.org organization

Curve25519-XSalsa20-Poly1305 is a combination of cryptographic methods used to exchange keys, encrypt data, and verify integrity.
customer data concept

A customer endpoint is a user's device or system, such as a laptop or server, that connects to a service or network.
also: customer endpoints, managed endpoint
Customer service contact details concept
Customer service contact details are phone numbers, email addresses, or other ways to reach support staff.
CVE vulnerability

CVE identifier concept
A CVE identifier is the standard public tracking number assigned to a known cybersecurity vulnerability.
CVEs concept
CVEs are standardized public identifiers for known cybersecurity vulnerabilities.
CVSS concept
CVSS is a standard scoring system used to rate how severe a software vulnerability is.
CVSS 9.3 concept
CVSS 9.3 is a very high vulnerability severity score on a 0-to-10 scale used to show how serious a security flaw is.
CVSS score concept
A CVSS score is a standard number used to show how severe a software vulnerability is.
CVSS v3.1 concept
CVSS v3.1 is a standard scoring system used to describe how serious a software vulnerability is.
also: CVSS vector
CVSS v4.0 concept
CVSS v4.0 is version 4.0 of the Common Vulnerability Scoring System, a standard way to rate how serious a vulnerability is.

CWE-94 is a software weakness category for improper control of code generation, often leading to code injection.
cyber concept
Cyber is a broad shorthand for things related to computers, networks, and digital security.
cyber extortion concept
Cyber extortion is when criminals use hacking, stolen data, or system disruption to pressure victims into paying money.
also: cyber extortion incidents
cyber incident concept
A cyber incident is any event where digital systems, accounts, or data may have been attacked, exposed, or disrupted.
Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act other
The Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act is a U.S. law requiring certain critical infrastructure organizations to report major cyber incidents.
cyber incidents concept
Cyber incidents are events that threaten or harm computer systems, networks, or data.
cyber risk concept
Cyber risk is the chance that digital systems, data, or operations could be harmed by security problems.
Cyber theft concept
Cyber theft is stealing money, data, or digital assets using computers or online access.
cyber threats concept
Cyber threats are possible dangers to computers, networks, or data caused by attackers or malicious software.
Cyber-espionage campaign concept
A cyber-espionage campaign is a planned hacking operation meant to secretly gather information from targets.
cyberattack concept
A cyberattack is an attempt to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems or data.
Cyberattack tools tool
Cyberattack tools are programs or scripts used to break into, disrupt, or steal from computer systems.

cyberattacks concept
Malicious activities conducted over computer networks to steal data, disrupt operations, or damage systems.
cybercrime group concept
A cybercrime group is an organized group that uses computers or the internet to commit crimes.
cybercriminals threat-actor
Cybercriminals are people who use computers or the internet to commit crimes such as fraud, theft, or extortion.
CyberGym product
CyberGym is a cybersecurity evaluation or training platform referenced in security reporting.
Cybersecurity concept
Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting computers, networks, software, and data from digital attacks or misuse.
Cybersecurity evaluations concept
Cybersecurity evaluations are reviews that measure how well systems, policies, or organizations are protected from cyber threats.
cybersecurity experts organization
Cybersecurity experts are people who specialize in protecting computers, networks, and data from attacks.
Cybersecurity gaps concept
Cybersecurity gaps are weaknesses or missing protections that could make systems easier to attack.
also: cyber gaps
cybersecurity incident concept
A cybersecurity incident is an event that threatens the security of systems, networks, or data.
Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act of 2015 other
The Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act of 2015 is a U.S. law meant to encourage organizations and government agencies to share cyber threat information.
also: CISA 2015
Cybersecurity mandates concept
Cybersecurity mandates are required rules or orders telling organizations what security measures they must follow.
Cybersecurity matter concept
A cybersecurity matter is an issue, investigation, or event involving the protection of computer systems or data.
Cybersecurity programs concept
Cybersecurity programs are organized efforts to protect an organization's systems, data, people, and operations from digital threats.
cybersecurity-and-infrastructure-security-agency organization

CyCognito is a cybersecurity company known for external attack surface management technology.
CyCognito Platform product

also: Dangleggedon, Dangle Day

also: dangling DNS infrastructure, dangling DNS domains, dangling DNS domains and subdomains
data breach concept
A data breach is an incident where sensitive, private, or protected information is accessed, exposed, or stolen without permission.
data centers concept
Data centers are facilities full of servers and networking equipment that run websites, cloud services, and business systems.
data exfiltration technique
Data exfiltration is the unauthorized removal or copying of data from a system.
also: Exfiltration, data exfiltration only
data exposure concept
Data exposure means sensitive information is left accessible to people or systems that should not be able to see it.
data extortion technique
A crime where attackers steal sensitive files and threaten to publish or sell them unless a ransom is paid.
data extortion group threat-actor
A data extortion group is a criminal group that steals or claims to steal data and demands payment to avoid leaking it.
data leak site tool

A data pipeline is an automated process that moves and transforms data from one place or system to another.
Data processing pipeline concept
A data processing pipeline is a series of automated steps that collects, transforms, and prepares data for use.
Data protection concept
Data protection means keeping information safe from loss, theft, exposure, or unauthorized changes.
Data sensitivity concept
Data sensitivity describes how carefully information must be protected based on the harm that could happen if it is exposed or changed.
data theft concept
Data theft is the stealing of information from a system or service.
data-theft-extortion technique
Data-theft-extortion is when criminals steal information and threaten to publish or sell it unless the victim pays.

Database credentials are usernames, passwords, keys, or tokens used to access a database.
dataset processing pipeline concept
A dataset processing pipeline is a series of automated steps that clean, transform, and prepare data for analysis or machine learning.
datasets concept
Datasets are collections of information that researchers or tools analyze to find patterns and evidence.
Debian product
A well-known community-driven Linux distribution famous for its stability and package management system.

Debug means to inspect software or systems to find and fix errors, and attackers can sometimes abuse debugging features to learn how something works.
decryption concept
Decryption is the process of turning scrambled encrypted data back into readable information.

DeepSeek organization
DeepSeek is an AI service provider referenced in the article.
DEF CON 2026 organization
DEF CON 2026 is a major hacker and cybersecurity conference planned for 2026.
def-con
DEF CON is a major annual hacker and cybersecurity conference in Las Vegas.
Defend concept
Defend means to protect systems, networks, data, or users from cyber threats.
Defender product
Defender usually refers to Microsoft Defender, Microsoft’s built-in security and antimalware product line.
Defender for Office 365 product
Microsoft Defender for Office 365 is a security product that protects email and collaboration tools from threats like phishing and malware.
defenders concept
Defenders are the people or teams responsible for protecting systems and responding to cyber threats.
defense evasion technique
Defense evasion means techniques attackers use to avoid being detected or blocked by security tools.
deleted concept
Deleted means removed from normal access, though copies may sometimes still exist in backups, logs, or recovery areas.
denial-of-service
Denial-of-service is an attack that overwhelms a system so legitimate users cannot access it.
denmark other
Denmark is a country in Northern Europe.
Department for Education organization
The Department for Education is the UK government department responsible for education and children's services in England.

The Department of Defense is the U.S. government department responsible for the military and national defense.
Department of Homeland Security organization
The Department of Homeland Security is a U.S. government department responsible for domestic security, including cyber defense.
Department of War organization
The Department of War is a government defense organization name referenced in policy or security reporting.
dependencies concept
Dependencies are outside software components that a project relies on to work.
dependencies concept
Dependencies are outside software components or libraries that an application needs in order to work.
dependency concept
A dependency is outside software that an application relies on, which can create risk if that outside component is vulnerable or malicious.
dependency lifecycle scripts technique
Dependency lifecycle scripts are commands that package managers run automatically during steps like install, build, or publish.
Detect technique
Detect means to identify suspicious or malicious activity in systems, networks, or data.
detection concept
Detection is the process of finding signs of suspicious or malicious activity.

Detection and analysis is the incident-response phase where teams identify alerts and determine what happened.

Detection rules are instructions security tools use to flag suspicious behavior or known attack patterns.
detections concept
Alerts or findings generated by security tools indicating that a potential threat or malicious activity has been identified.
developer workflows concept
Developer workflows are the regular steps software developers use to write, test, review, and release code.
DfE Help Desk Self-Service Portal product
The DfE Help Desk Self-Service Portal is an online support portal for the UK Department for Education.

Dharma ransomware is a malware family that encrypts victims' files and demands payment to restore access.
diffpatch tool

also: diffpatch route
diffpatch-api tool
diffpatch-api is a software package or API referenced in security reporting.

disruption concept

domestic end product concept

downtime concept

dragonforce

Drinking Water and Clean Water State Revolving Funds other

edge devices concept

ehdgmsrd.com other
ehdgmsrd.com is a domain name referenced in security reporting.

Elastic Stack 9.3.0+ product
Elastic Stack 9.3.0+ refers to version 9.3.0 and later of Elastic's search, logging, analytics, and security data platform.
also: Stack 9.3.0+

Higher access rights than a standard user, allowing actions like installing software or modifying system files.

encoding concept
Encoding is changing data into a particular format so computers can store, send, or interpret it.

Encrypted data is information that has been scrambled so it cannot be read without the right key.
encryption concept
Encryption is a way of scrambling information so only someone with the right key can read it.
end to end concept
End to end means something is handled across the whole process from start to finish, often without gaps between steps.
endpoint concept
An endpoint is a user device such as a laptop, phone, or server that connects to a network.

endpoints concept

ENISA's Multilayer Framework for Good Cybersecurity Practices for AI is European guidance for securing artificial intelligence systems across multiple layers.

Enki WhiteHat organization
Enki WhiteHat is a named security organization, researcher identity, or tool referenced in security reporting.
EnPortv.sys tool

Enterprise services concept
Enterprise services are business IT systems or applications used across an organization.
environment variables concept
Environment variables are named settings stored by an operating system or runtime that programs can read while they run.

EPA organization

equipment authorization concept

event logs concept

executable concept
An executable is a file that can run as a program on a computer.

exfiltrated technique

Exfiltrates means secretly takes data out of a system or network without permission.

exploit code tool

Exploitability concept
Exploitability describes how easily an attacker can take advantage of a security weakness.
exploitation technique
Exploitation is taking advantage of a weakness in software or people to gain unauthorized access or control.

Exploitation in the wild means attackers are actively using a vulnerability against real targets, not just testing it in a lab.
exploited in the wild concept
Exploited in the wild means attackers are actively using a vulnerability against real targets, not just in a lab.

Exploits technique
Exploits are code or techniques that take advantage of software vulnerabilities.

extortion payments concept

federal agencies organization

The Federal Communications Commission is the U.S. agency that regulates radio, television, wire, satellite, and cable communications.

file exfiltration technique

Malicious dataset technique
A malicious dataset is a data collection designed to trick software or AI systems into running harmful actions when it is opened or processed.
Malicious File concept
A malicious file is a file designed to harm a computer, steal information, or help an attacker gain access.
Malicious functionality concept
Malicious functionality is code behavior intentionally designed to harm systems, steal data, or help an attacker.
malicious package malware
A malicious package is a software package that contains harmful code or was created to trick users into installing it.
malicious page concept
A malicious page is a web page designed to trick users, steal information, or attack their device.
malicious software concept
Malicious software is software designed to harm systems, steal information, or give attackers control.
malicious traffic concept
Malicious traffic is harmful network activity sent to or from systems.
Malicious update technique
A malicious update is a software update that has been tampered with to install harmful code.
Malicious updates technique
Malicious updates are software updates that have been tampered with or designed to install harmful code.
malvertising technique
Malvertising is the use of online ads to spread scams, malware, or links to dangerous websites.

A malvertising campaign is an attack that uses online advertisements to lead people to scams, malware, or phishing pages.
malware concept
Malware is software made to harm, spy on, or take control of computers or data.

Malware campaigns concept
Malware campaigns are coordinated waves of attacks that spread malicious software to targets.
malware delivery technique
Malware delivery is the process attackers use to get malicious software onto a victim's device.
malware families concept
Malware families are groups of related malicious programs that share code, behavior, or a common creator.
malware infection concept
A malware infection happens when harmful software gets onto a device or system and can run there.
Manage concept
Manage is a security function category focused on running, maintaining, and governing cybersecurity activities.
Managed service providers organization
Managed service providers are companies that run or support another organization’s IT systems for them.
also: MSPs, managed service provider
management interface concept
A management interface is a control panel or network access point used to administer a system or device.
management interfaces tool
Management interfaces are control screens or APIs used to configure and administer systems, devices, or applications.

A Management Server is a central system administrators use to configure and control other systems or security devices.
Management system product
A management system is software used to configure, monitor, and control devices, users, or services.
Manufacturing sector organization
The manufacturing sector includes companies that make physical goods and is often considered important infrastructure in cybersecurity.
map concept
In software and web-server configuration, a map is a rule or data structure that links one value to another.
masquerading
Masquerading is when attackers disguise malicious files, processes, or accounts to look legitimate.

MCP, or Model Context Protocol, is a standard way for AI assistants to connect to external tools, files, and services.

An MCP Server is a server that implements the Model Context Protocol to connect AI systems with tools, data, or services.
mcp-servers

also: Measure function
medusa

MedusaHVNC is a remote-control malware or tool that can let an attacker secretly view and control a victim's computer.
memory corruption vulnerability

memory safety concept

MeshAgent is a remote management agent used with MeshCentral to control and administer devices over the internet.
Metadata concept
Metadata is data that describes other data, such as when a file was created, who sent an email, or where a photo was taken.
mexico
Mexico is a North American country that may appear in cybersecurity reporting as a location, target, or government context.

MFA is the shortened name for multi-factor authentication, a login process that uses more than one proof of identity.

microsoft organization

Microsoft Azure product

Microsoft Copilot product

Microsoft SQL Server is Microsoft's database server software used to store and manage data.

Microsoft Windows product
Microsoft Windows is a widely used operating system for personal computers and servers.
Microsoft Word product

microsoft-365
Microsoft 365 is Microsoft’s cloud productivity and security suite including Office apps, email, storage, and collaboration tools.
microsoft-teams
Microsoft Teams is Microsoft’s workplace chat, meeting, and collaboration platform.
also: Teams

Misconfigurations vulnerability
Misconfigurations are incorrect settings that can accidentally expose systems or make attacks easier.
misuse concept

mitigations concept
Mitigations are steps taken to reduce the chance or impact of a security problem.

also: ATLAS
MITRE ATT&CK tool
MITRE ATT&CK is a framework for naming and organizing attacker techniques.
also: ATT&CK
mobile network concept

mobile phone numbers concept
Mobile phone numbers are personal contact numbers that can be sensitive because attackers may use them for scams or account takeover attempts.

mongodb product

moved laterally technique

msaRAT malware
msaRAT is a remote access trojan malware family referenced in security reporting.

multi-factor authentication concept
Multi-factor authentication is a login method that asks users to prove who they are in more than one way.

Multi-stage payloads are attacks that deliver malware in several steps instead of all at once.

ncsc organization

NERC CIP concept

netherlands

network traffic concept

new-york
New York is a U.S. state often mentioned in cybersecurity stories involving companies, victims, laws, or courts.
new-zealand other

night-rang3r other
night-rang3r is a security researcher or online alias referenced in security reporting.

Node product
Node usually refers to Node.js, a runtime that lets JavaScript run outside a web browser.

non-human identities concept
Non-human identities are digital identities used by systems, services, or automated processes instead of people.

north-korea other

November 2025 other
November 2025 is a calendar month referenced as a date or timeframe.
npm product

obfuscated technique

obfuscation technique
The technique of making code or data deliberately hard to understand to avoid detection by security tools.

OctLurk threat-actor
OctLurk is a threat-actor group referenced in security reporting.

online services concept

open internet concept

open registration concept

open source concept

Open source software concept

oracle

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is Oracle’s cloud computing platform for running applications, databases, storage, and networks.
also: Cloud Infrastructure

oversight concept

pace concept

password resets concept

patched concept

patches concept
Patches are software updates that fix bugs, security flaws, or other problems.
patching concept

payload concept

payloads concept

phishing technique

plugin concept

plugins concept

pOliCI tool

prompts concept

public services concept

QR codes are square barcodes that a phone camera can scan to open a link or read stored information.
QR-code phishing technique
QR-code phishing is a scam technique that uses QR codes to send people to fake or malicious websites.
Quick Assist tool
Quick Assist is a Microsoft remote support tool that lets one person view or control another Windows computer with permission.
ransom concept
A sum of money demanded by criminals to restore access to data or systems after a ransomware attack.
ransom negotiations concept
Ransom negotiations are discussions between a victim and criminals over payment demands after an attack such as ransomware or data theft.
ransom notes concept
Ransom notes are messages from attackers demanding payment, usually after data has been encrypted or stolen.
ransom payment concept
A ransom payment is money paid to criminals, often after a ransomware attack, in hopes of getting data restored or preventing leaks.
ransom payments concept
Ransom payments are money paid to criminals in hopes of recovering data, stopping leaks, or restoring access after an attack.
Ransom-ISAC organization
Ransom-ISAC is an information-sharing organization name referenced in ransomware-related security reporting.
ransomware concept
Ransomware is malicious software or an operation that locks or steals data to pressure victims into paying money.
ransomware activity concept
Ransomware activity is behavior related to malware that locks or steals data and demands payment from victims.
ransomware attacks technique
Ransomware attacks are incidents where attackers use software or methods to disrupt access and demand payment.
ransomware gangs threat-actor
Criminal groups that use malicious software to encrypt victims' data and demand payment for its release.
ransomware group threat-actor
A ransomware group is a criminal or threat-actor team that uses malware to lock or steal data and demand payment.
ransomware operations threat-actor
Ransomware operations are organized criminal activities that break into systems, encrypt or steal data, and demand payment.
ransomware operators threat-actor
Ransomware operators are criminals who run attacks that lock or steal data and demand payment from victims.
Ransomware-as-a-service model concept
The ransomware-as-a-service model is a criminal business setup where ransomware developers rent their tools to other attackers for a share of the profits.
also: RaaS schemes
RDP protocol
RDP is Microsoft’s Remote Desktop Protocol, which lets someone control a Windows computer over a network.
reachability concept
Reachability means whether one system, account, or network location can access another.
README files concept
README files are text files that explain what a project or download is and how to use it.
Real time concept
Real time means something happens or is shown immediately, or with very little delay.
recommendation concept
A recommendation is suggested guidance or an action that someone should consider taking to reduce risk or solve a problem.
Red Menshen malware
Red Menshen is a malware family referenced in security reporting, associated with stealthy backdoor access to targeted systems.
red teaming technique
Red teaming is an authorized exercise where security experts act like attackers to test an organization's defenses.
RedAlert malware
RedAlert is a ransomware family referenced in security reporting.
redirect concept
A redirect sends a browser or request from one web address to another.
redirects concept
Redirects are instructions that automatically send a user or browser from one web address to another.
Reenter technique
Reenter means to call back into code before an earlier execution of that code has finished, which can cause security problems.
Reentrancy vulnerability
Reentrancy is a smart-contract bug pattern where a contract is called again before the first call finishes, possibly allowing theft or logic abuse.
Regional account directory concept
A regional account directory is a location-specific directory that stores user or account information for a region.
Registry concept
The Registry is a Windows database that stores system and application settings.
Registry-based payload storage technique
Registry-based payload storage hides malware data inside the Windows Registry instead of normal files.
relay concept
A relay is a server or service that forwards network traffic or email from one place to another.
remediation technique
Remediation is the work of fixing a security problem and reducing the damage it caused.
remote access concept
The ability to connect to another computer or network from a distant location and use it as if you were physically present.
Remote access tools tool
Remote access tools let someone control or manage a computer from another location, which can be legitimate or abused by attackers.
remote code execution flaw vulnerability
A remote code execution flaw is a serious bug that can let an attacker run commands on a system from somewhere else over a network.
Remote code execution vulnerability vulnerability
A remote code execution vulnerability is a flaw that can let an attacker run commands on a system from afar.
Remote Desktop concept
A technology that lets you see and control a computer's desktop from another device over a network.
Remote Desktop Protocol protocol
Remote Desktop Protocol is a Microsoft protocol that lets someone control a Windows computer over a network.
Remote management software tool
Remote management software lets someone administer or control a computer over a network.
remote management tools tool
Remote management tools let administrators control, monitor, or fix computers from another location, but attackers can also abuse them.
remote-code-execution technique
Remote code execution is a serious flaw that lets an attacker run commands on a system from elsewhere.
Remotely tool
Remotely is a remote administration tool that can be used to access and manage computers over a network.
RemSupp tool
RemSupp is a remote support tool or component referenced in security reporting that may be abused for unauthorized access.
repositories concept
Repositories are places where software project files and related development data are stored.
repository concept
A repository is a storage location for code, files, and their change history, especially in systems like GitHub.
Repository write access concept
Repository write access is permission to change code or files in a software repository.
also: repository write grants
reputation scanners tool
Reputation scanners are security services that judge whether a file, link, domain, or IP address looks trustworthy based on past activity and reputation data.
researchers organization
Researchers are people who study systems, threats, or vulnerabilities to understand and improve security.
resilience concept
The ability of an organization to anticipate, withstand, and recover from adverse cyber events and security breaches.
Respond technique
Respond means to take action after detecting a security issue, such as containing an attack or fixing affected systems.
REST API protocol
A REST API is a common way for software systems to request and exchange data over the web.
Restart concept
A restart is turning a device or program off and then back on again to refresh it or apply changes.
Restore technique
Restore means to bring data, settings, or a system back to an earlier working state.
reverse engineering technique
Reverse engineering is taking software apart to understand how it works without relying on the original source code.
reverse proxy tool
A reverse proxy is a server that sits in front of other servers and forwards user requests to them, often adding security or load balancing.
Risk and Resilience Assessment concept
A Risk and Resilience Assessment is a review that identifies threats, weaknesses, and ways an organization can keep operating during disruptions.
also: RRA, RRAs, Risk and Resilience Assessments
risk assessment concept
Risk assessment is the process of judging how likely and serious a security problem may be.
Risk mitigation concept
Risk mitigation means taking steps to reduce the chance or impact of something bad happening.
RMM tool
Software tools used by IT teams to manage computers remotely, sometimes abused by attackers to maintain persistent control over infected machines.
also: RMM tools, RMM platforms
rogue femtocell tool
A rogue femtocell is an unauthorized or malicious small cellular base station that can interfere with or spy on nearby mobile devices.
root access concept
Having complete administrative control over a computer or network, allowing unrestricted system changes.
Root code execution technique
Root code execution means an attacker can run commands with the highest level of control on a Unix-like system.
also: unauthenticated root code execution
Roundcube Webmail product
Roundcube Webmail is an open-source webmail application used to read and manage email through a browser.
Royal malware
Royal is a ransomware group and malware family known for extorting organizations after encrypting their data.
run code concept
To run code means to make a computer execute instructions written in a programming language.
rundll32.exe tool
rundll32.exe is a legitimate Windows program that runs code from DLL files, but attackers often abuse it to launch malicious code while looking normal.
Runtime enumeration technique
Runtime enumeration means listing available objects, services, users, or settings while a program is running.
russia
Russia is a country frequently referenced in cybersecurity stories involving cybercrime groups, espionage, and government activity.
Russian hackers threat-actor
Russian hackers are cyber attackers or groups described as operating from Russia or being linked to Russian interests.
Russian threat actors threat-actor
Russian threat actors are hacking groups or individuals linked to Russia or Russian interests in security reporting.
SaaS concept
SaaS is software delivered over the internet as a subscription or hosted service instead of installed and managed entirely by the customer.
SaaS accounts concept
SaaS accounts are user accounts for cloud software services accessed over the internet.
SaaS applications concept
SaaS applications are software services delivered over the internet rather than installed and managed locally by each organization.
SaaS apps concept
SaaS apps are software services used through the internet instead of being installed and managed entirely on your own computer.
SaaS logs concept
SaaS logs are records of activity from cloud software services, such as sign-ins, settings changes, and data access.
SaaS platforms product
SaaS platforms are online software services that users access through the internet rather than installing locally.
SaaS security concept
SaaS security is the practice of protecting cloud applications and the data, users, and settings inside them.
SaaS supply chain attack technique
A SaaS supply chain attack compromises a cloud software provider, integration, or dependency to reach that provider's customers.
also: SaaS supply chain attacks
Safe active query technique
Safe active query is a security idea for allowing a system to ask or test something actively without exposing unsafe data or behavior.
Safe Drinking Water Act other
The Safe Drinking Water Act is a U.S. law that sets standards for the safety of public drinking water.
also: SDWA, SDWA 1433
SafeCallback tool
SafeCallback is a smart-contract or software component name referenced in security reporting.
safeguards concept
Safeguards are protections put in place to reduce the chance or impact of harm, misuse, or security incidents.
safety guardrails concept
Safety guardrails are rules or controls designed to stop a system, especially AI, from doing unsafe or unwanted things.
salesforce product
Salesforce is a cloud platform for customer relationship management, sales, service, and business applications.
Samba product
Samba is open-source software that lets Linux and Unix systems share files and directory services with Windows networks.
Samba Active Directory Domain Controller product
Samba Active Directory Domain Controller is a Samba server role that provides Windows-style domain login and directory services.
Samba Team organization
The Samba Team is the open-source group that develops and maintains the Samba file and directory services software.
same-day-domain concept
A same-day-domain is a domain that was registered very recently, often on the same day it is used, which can be a warning sign in phishing or spam campaigns.
sandbox concept
A sandbox is an isolated environment used to run code more safely so it cannot easily affect the rest of the system.
sandbox-escape technique
A technique where malware breaks out of a restricted, isolated testing environment to attack the real underlying system.
also: escaped OpenAI’s research environment, escaped a constrained research sandbox
sandboxes tool
Sandboxes are isolated environments used to safely run and observe suspicious files or programs without risking a real system.
sandboxing technique
Sandboxing means running a file or program in an isolated environment so it can be observed safely without risking the real system.
Sapphire Sleet threat-actor
Sapphire Sleet is a North Korean state-sponsored hacking group identified by Microsoft.
SapphireSleet threat-actor
SapphireSleet is a North Korea-linked threat actor known for cyber-espionage and financially motivated activity.
Scam technique
A scam is a dishonest scheme designed to trick people into giving up money, information, or access.
scammers threat-actor
Scammers are people who trick others to steal money, information, or access.
scams concept
Scams are dishonest schemes designed to trick people into giving money, information, or access.
scanner tool
A scanner is a tool that searches for information or problems automatically.
Scanners tool
Scanners are tools that check systems, networks, or websites for exposed services, weaknesses, or signs of compromise.
scanning technique
Scanning is checking computers, networks, or services to find what is reachable and what may be vulnerable.
scans concept
Scans are automated checks that examine software or related data for issues or information.
Scattered Spider threat-actor
Scattered Spider is a cybercrime group known for social engineering, account theft, and high-profile intrusions.
scheduled-tasks
Scheduled tasks are automated jobs on a computer that attackers can abuse to run malware at specific times or after reboot.
scope concept
scope defines what access, targets, or permissions are included in a security test, login request, or authorization grant.
scopes concept
Scopes define the boundaries where a permission applies.
Scoping concept
Scoping is deciding what systems, data, people, or issues are included in a project, investigation, or assessment.
screen-capture technique
Screen capture is the act of taking an image or recording of what is shown on a device's screen.
scripts tool
Scripts are small sets of commands that automate tasks a computer should perform.
also: script, operational scripts, operational scripting
second stage technique
A second stage is follow-up malware or code that is downloaded or run after an initial infection succeeds.
secret argument concept
A secret argument is a hidden command-line option or input value that changes how a program behaves.
Secure Preferences concept
Secure Preferences is a Chromium browser file that stores protected user and extension settings.
Securing AI concept
Securing AI means protecting artificial intelligence systems from misuse, manipulation, data leaks, and unsafe behavior.
Securities and Exchange Commission organization
The Securities and Exchange Commission is the U.S. government agency that regulates securities markets and public company disclosures.
security advisory concept
A security advisory is a notice that explains a security problem, who is affected, and what users should do about it.
Security bugs vulnerability
Security bugs are software flaws that can let attackers do something they should not be able to do.
security controls concept
Security controls are safeguards, such as settings, tools, or policies, used to reduce risk.
Security Impact Rating concept
Security Impact Rating is a score or label used to describe how serious a security issue may be.
also: SIR
Security incident concept
A security incident is an event where systems, data, or accounts may have been attacked, exposed, or misused.
security patch concept
A security patch is a software update that fixes a vulnerability or weakness attackers could exploit.
Security patch plugin tool
A security patch plugin is an add-on that helps apply or manage fixes for security weaknesses in software.
security software product
Security software is software designed to protect computers, networks, or data from threats.
security teams concept
Groups of professionals responsible for protecting an organization's information, systems, and networks from cyber threats.
security testing concept
Security testing is checking software, systems, or networks to find weaknesses before attackers can exploit them.
security tools tool
Security tools are software or hardware products used to detect, prevent, investigate, or respond to cyber threats.
security updates concept
Security updates are software fixes that close vulnerabilities or improve protection against threats.
Security vulnerabilities vulnerability
Security vulnerabilities are weaknesses in software, hardware, or processes that attackers can exploit.
self-made device tool
A self-made device is hardware built or modified by an individual rather than bought as a standard commercial product.
self-migrating C2 technique
Self-migrating C2 describes attacker command-and-control infrastructure that can automatically move to new servers or addresses to stay reachable and avoid takedown.
Self-migrating command-and-control technique
Self-migrating command-and-control is an attacker control setup that can automatically move to new infrastructure to stay reachable or avoid shutdown.
SelfSubjectRulesReview protocol
SelfSubjectRulesReview is a Kubernetes API feature that lets a user or workload ask what actions it is allowed to perform.
also: Self-Subject Review
Semantic Layer concept
A semantic layer is a business-friendly data layer that gives consistent meaning to data across tools and applications.
Semiconductor concept
A semiconductor is a material used to make computer chips and other electronic components.
sensing concept
Sensing means detecting or monitoring what is happening in a system, network, or environment.
sensitive data concept
Sensitive data is information that could cause harm if exposed, such as passwords, financial details, or medical records.
sensitive information concept
Sensitive information is data that should be protected because exposing it could harm a person, company, or system.
server process concept
A server process is a running program that waits for requests from users, devices, or other programs and responds to them.
service accounts concept
Service accounts are accounts used by software or systems rather than by individual people.
service providers organization
Service providers are companies or organizations that deliver services such as internet access, hosting, software platforms, or managed IT support.

session tokens concept
Session tokens are temporary digital values that prove a user is already logged in to a website or service.

Shadow IT is technology used inside an organization without official approval or oversight from the IT department.
Shai Rod other
Shai Rod is a named individual referenced in the security story.
also: NightRang3r
shared infrastructure concept
Shared infrastructure is computing or network equipment used by multiple services, customers, or attackers.
shell tool
A shell is a command-line interface that lets a user or program run commands on a computer.
shellcode technique
Shellcode is small code used in exploits to make a vulnerable program run attacker-controlled commands.
shinyhunters

ShinyHunters threat-actor
ShinyHunters is a cybercriminal group known for data theft, extortion, and selling stolen information.
ShinyHunters extortion gang threat-actor
ShinyHunters is a cybercriminal group known for data theft and extortion.

SIGNBT malware

The signed portion is the part of a message, file, or URL protected by a digital signature to show it was not changed.
also: signed region
Significant cyber incidents concept
Significant cyber incidents are serious security events that cause major disruption, data loss, or risk to important systems.
Silent Push’s Dangling DNS API product
Silent Push’s Dangling DNS API is a service for finding domain records that may be vulnerable to dangling-DNS takeover.
also: Dangling DNS API
Silent Ransom threat-actor
Silent Ransom is a threat-actor name referenced in security reporting, likely associated with extortion or ransomware activity.
also: Silent Ransomware
silent-push organization
Silent Push is a threat intelligence company that tracks internet infrastructure used by attackers.
also: Silent Push research team, Silent Push Platform, Silent Push data set
SilkLurk threat-actor
SilkLurk is a threat-actor group referenced in security reporting.
Silver Fox threat-actor
Silver Fox is a named threat actor referenced in security reporting.
singapore
Singapore is a Southeast Asian country and technology hub often referenced in cybersecurity reporting.

Size calculation is the process of computing how much memory, data, or space something needs, which can cause bugs if done wrong.
Slackware product
Slackware is a long-running Linux distribution used as an operating system.

Slopsquatting is an attack where criminals register package names, domains, or links that AI tools have hallucinated so people may mistakenly use them.
SMA organization
SMA is a company that makes solar inverters and energy-management equipment.

SMS protocol
SMS is the standard text messaging service used on mobile phones.
Snowflake product
Snowflake is a cloud data platform used to store and analyze data.
social engineering technique
Social engineering is manipulation of people into doing something or sharing information they otherwise would not.
social engineering attacks technique
Social engineering attacks are tricks that manipulate people into revealing information or doing something unsafe.
Socially engineering technique
Socially engineering means manipulating people into revealing information or taking unsafe actions.
socks5.exe tool
socks5.exe is an executable name that usually suggests a SOCKS5 proxy tool used to route network traffic.
SoftPerfect Network Scanner tool
SoftPerfect Network Scanner is a tool used to discover devices and services on a network.

Software flaws are mistakes or weaknesses in programs that can cause bugs or create security risks.
software maintainers concept
Software maintainers are the people or teams responsible for updating, fixing, and managing a software project.
software supply chain concept
The software supply chain is the set of code, libraries, tools, and vendors involved in building and delivering software.
software supply-chain compromise concept

Solaris product
Solaris is a Unix-based operating system originally developed by Sun Microsystems and later owned by Oracle.
SonicWall organization
SonicWall is a cybersecurity vendor known for firewalls, secure remote access, and network security products.
Sophos organization
Sophos is a cybersecurity company that sells security products and publishes threat research.
Sorella Angstrom other
Sorella Angstrom is a named entity referenced in security reporting, likely an organization, researcher, or project.
source code concept
The human-readable code written by programmers that makes up software.
source IP addresses concept
Source IP addresses identify where network traffic appears to come from.
south-africa other
South Africa is a country that may be mentioned as a location or target in a security story.
south-korea
South Korea is an East Asian country often referenced in cybersecurity stories involving technology, espionage, or regional threats.
spain other
Spain is a country in southwestern Europe.
spear-phishing technique

spearphishing technique
Spearphishing is a targeted scam message sent to a specific person or group to trick them into giving access or information.
also: spearphishing campaigns

also: SQL APIs

A SQL injection vulnerability is a weakness that lets attackers put database commands into an app to view, change, or delete data.

SSH key concept

STAC4749 is a named threat-activity cluster referenced in security reporting.

A stack is a set of technologies, software layers, or components that work together to run an application or service.
STARDUST CHOLLIMA threat-actor

also: SLCGP

also: sanitary-survey mandate
state-backed actors threat-actor

Static binary analysis means examining a compiled program without running it to understand what it does or find flaws.
static credentials concept

Static user credentials are fixed usernames, passwords, keys, or tokens that do not change automatically.

stolen credentials concept

stolen data concept

stolen records concept

Struggle is a malware family, tool, or threat name referenced in security reporting.
subdomain concept

supply chain concept
A supply chain is the network of vendors, software, services, and processes an organization depends on to operate.

Supply chains are the outside vendors, software, services, and dependencies an organization relies on to operate.
supply-chain-attacks technique

taiwan other

takedown technique

TeamCity 2017.1+ product

telecommunications concept

templates concept

tenable

threat actor threat-actor
